assumptions.description: The dimensions $m,n$ are public and the matrix is hidden. Both strategy domains are compact and convex, ensuring a saddle point.

model.parameter_domain_description: $\varepsilon$: positive real; $m$: positive integer; $n$: positive integer. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $B_2^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_2\le1\}$, and $\Delta_m=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:y_i\ge0,\ \mathbf1^\top y=1\}$. Also $X=B_2^n$, with each row satisfying $\|A_{i,:}\|_2\le1$.
The dimensions $m,n$ are public and the matrix is hidden. Both strategy domains are compact and convex, ensuring a saddle point.

description_paragraphs: Public inputs include matrix dimensions $m,n$ and tolerance $\varepsilon$, together with the declared initial point and feasible-set information. The hidden function, operator, or matrix has no disclosed analytic representation.

objects.definition: Access an unknown normalized matrix through left and right multiplication by arbitrary real vectors, and return feasible approximate Nash strategies. The native complexity is the fixed call budget needed for the gap tolerance and instancewise success probability.
The feasible set is explicitly public. Exact projections and linear algebra use known geometry and reveal no hidden-function information.

domains.definition: The explicit domain of each operation’s query_signature.

Return $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in X\times\Delta_m$. Any measurable transcript postprocessing is allowed, including unqueried points, averages, and convex combinations, subject to the declared output domain and feasibility. No extra function value or computable certificate is required.

norms.definition: Use the Euclidean vector norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$.

proofs.title: Return any public feasible strategy
proofs.body: Under the declared matrix normalization and strategy domains, every feasible bilinear payoff lies in $[-1,1]$. The difference between its maximum against a fixed minimizing strategy and its minimum against a fixed maximizing strategy is therefore at most two. Return any publicly specified feasible strategy pair without querying. It meets every tolerance $\varepsilon\ge2$ deterministically. Nonnegativity of query cost certifies exact zero cost.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.
